newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA TOO STRONG FOR SPRINGBOKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA TOO STRONG FOR SPRINGBOKS.

text.p: Australia revived their Tri-Nations campaign and cheered besieged coach Greg Smith with a resounding 32-20 victory over South Africa on Saturday.

One week after they were thoroughly outplayed in a 33-18 defeat by Tri-Nations leaders New Zealand in Melbourne -- prompting speculation about Smith's future -- Australia proved too committed and inventive for the World Cup holders.
By scoring four tries to three the home side also gave Smith some breathing space after he publicly acknowledged that defeat on Saturday could cost him his job.
It was Australia's highest winning score in a test against the Springboks, eclipsing their 28-20 success in 1993.
Ironically, veteran flyhalf David Knox, previously written-off by Smith as a "non-tackler" and a defensive liability, played a pivotal role in the victory.
Knox, recalled from a playing stint with South African province Natal as a replacement for the injured Tim Horan, invigorated Australia's backline in which winger Ben Tune excelled with two tries.
Knox, 34 this month, also proved a capable goalkicker in the absence of injured fullback Matt Burke, landing three conversions and two penalties.

The Wallabies benefited from some feeble and half-hearted Springbok defence in scoring four early tries to virtually wrap up the match before halftime. A succession of tackles were missed as Australia built a 26-10 lead at the interval.
Knox set up the opening score for fullback and ACT Brumbies team mate Stephen Larkham in the eighth minute with a well-timed pass near the corner.
Winger and man-of-the-match Tune also benefited from Knox's vision and quick delivery to score his two tries at the end of intricate moves in the 19th and 40th minutes.
Although their attacking play showed a marked improvement on their stodgy, limited performance against the All Blacks, poor Springbok defending made things easier.
In between Tune's two scores, number eight Daniel Manu charged through unmolested to score under the posts from a line-out won by inspirational captain John Eales.

South Africa's lone reply before halftime resulted from an Australian lack of discipline as much as their own efforts when backchat by Gregan brought a reversal of a penalty five metres from the Australian line.
Huge prop Os du Randt collected a short pass from the tap start and barged over from close range. Flyhalf Jannie de Beer, who earlier kicked a penalty, landed the conversion.
In a strangely lethargic performance, the Springboks at no stage played with the intensity that stretched New Zealand before they went down 35-32 in the series opener two weeks ago.

With 15 minutes to go, lock Mark Andrews narrowed the scoreline with South Africa's second try, finishing off a break by flanker Ruben Kruger, and in the final minute De Beer dived over for another consolation.
Smith, whose second 12-month contract expires at the end of 1997, has been criticised over his tactics and a lack of consistency in team selection.
His position will be reviewed at the end of the Tri-Nations series, leaving open the possibility of a change before the tour to Argentina and Britain during the northern hemisphere autumn.

For South Africa, who have now followed a home series defeat by the British Lions with two successive Tri-Nations reversals, next week's daunting trip to New Zealand offers little hope of a change of fortunes.
Teams:

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Daniel Manu (22-Troy Coker, 56), 7-David Wilson, 6-Matt Cockbain (19-Brett Robinson 58), 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Owen Finegan, 3-Andrew Heath (20-Andrew Blades, 71), 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw; 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Otto, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt (20-Adrian Garvey, 61).
